data.title: Meet Bhanuka Harischandra, Director of Inspire College
data.excerpt: Meet Bhanuka Harischandra, Director of Inspire College, founder of Surge Global and a Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia honouree. Explore his journey from building a YouTube network for esports creators to leading the formation of Short Circuit Group.
content:
Bhanuka Harischandra, Director of Inspire College, is a self-taught Sri Lankan entrepreneur who builds businesses through technology, data and digital strategy. He founded Surge Global and went on to become Group Managing Director of Short Circuit Group. His career began in a different corner of the digital economy, helping esports creators turn their YouTube audiences into income.
From esports to Surge Global
As a teenager, Bhanuka founded TheGamersCottage, a YouTube multichannel network that helped more than 600 creators monetise over half a billion esports video views. He learned how creators attract audiences, how to tell whether content is reaching the right people and how to build a business around that attention. Working in a fast-changing industry also shaped his approach to entrepreneurship. He learned to test ideas early, pay attention to the results and adapt when something did not work as expected. restofworld.org

He took those lessons into Surge Global, a firm that brought together design, marketing and technology. Surge attracted strategic investment connected to the Tavistock Group in 2018 and went on to work with clients ranging from startups to global companies. The work gave Bhanuka a chance to apply the same principles he had learned with creators to larger organisations facing more complex questions about how to reach customers and grow online. www.icta.lk
Building Short Circuit Group
Bhanuka led the merger of Surge Global and Calcey Technologies to form Short Circuit Group. The merger combined Calcey’s software engineering expertise with Surge’s capabilities in growth, design and data. With those disciplines working together, the group can help clients define what they need, design and build the technology, and support its rollout. echelon.lk

As Group Managing Director, Bhanuka has spoken about building products alongside clients and sharing some of the commercial risk. This approach gives both sides a stake in how well the product performs after launch. It also brings the people responsible for engineering, design and growth into the conversation early, while decisions about what to build and whom it should serve are still being made. www.linkedin.com
Recognition and his role at Inspire College
Bhanuka is a TEDx speaker and was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia Class of 2021. Rest of World also included him in its RoW100: Global Tech’s Changemakers list, highlighting his work at Surge Global and as co-founder of Watchdog, a Sri Lankan fact-checking and open-source research collective. www.icta.lk

At Inspire College, Bhanuka brings the perspective of a founder who has built teams across creative and technical disciplines. His career offers students a practical example of how those skills come together. The work of growing a creator network, building a digital business or leading a technology group all starts with understanding what people need, testing ideas against evidence and bringing together people with the skills to act on what they learn.

data.title: A Smarter Way to Learn: Introducing Our New LMS
data.excerpt: Inspire College introduces a new Learning Management System for a smarter, more engaging online learning experience.
content: Knowing what to study next can make a real difference when you’re learning online. A student preparing for a first assignment, a working professional returning to study after a busy week, and a learner revising for an assessment all need a clear place to begin. Inspire College is introducing its new Learning Management System (LMS) to give students a clearer way to navigate their studies and build confidence as they progress.
A clearer way to manage online study

The LMS is the digital space where students engage with their courses. Students can use it to find their learning materials, see what they need to work on and keep track of their studies. For someone balancing classes with work or family responsibilities, it can be easier to use a short study session well when they know which topic to revisit or which task needs their attention.

That structure is especially useful when students are new to online learning. The first few weeks of a programme involve getting familiar with how a course is taught, what lecturers expect and how assessments are organised. A familiar place to return to can help students develop a routine and spend more of their time on the work itself.
Building confidence through practice

Confidence grows when students have opportunities to try something, see where they need more practice and return to it with a better understanding. The Inspire College OS demo shows how interactive simulations could support that process. It showcases scenarios that learners can work through individually or in groups, giving them a space to apply concepts, make decisions and discuss how they reached a result.

The demo also showcases an AI study coach and daily planning tools. A student who feels unsure where to start could use a study plan to break a broad goal, such as preparing for an assessment, into smaller tasks. They might begin by revisiting a topic, move on to a practice exercise and then identify a question to take back to their lecturer. The simulations, AI coach and planning tools are features showcased in the Inspire College OS demo.
Staying connected while learning online

Learning independently also means knowing when to ask for help. A student may understand the material but still want to clarify an assignment brief, check their interpretation of a concept or hear how someone else approached an exercise. The Inspire College OS demo explores ways to support those interactions through messaging and open-office Q&A. These are examples of how an online campus can give students more opportunities to raise questions and stay connected to the people supporting their learning.
A more confident next step

For Inspire College, a smarter way to learn starts with making the next step clear. Sometimes that means finding the right material before class. Sometimes it means practising a concept before submitting an assignment or knowing what to ask when a topic feels unfamiliar. When students can take those steps with greater confidence, they are better placed to build a study routine that works for them.
If you’re an Inspire College student, visit the Student Portal to access the LMS and check your course information.

data.title: Akbar Brothers Invests in the Future of Education
data.excerpt: Akbar Brothers has agreed to invest LKR 175 million in Inspire College to expand access to flexible online higher education across Sri Lanka.
content: Colombo, Sri Lanka · 20 November 2026

Akbar Brothers has agreed to invest LKR 175 million in Inspire College, backing its mission to make globally recognised higher education more accessible across Sri Lanka. The investment will support improvements to the college’s online learning platform, simplify how new students get started, and extend outreach to communities beyond the country’s major cities.

For many Sri Lankans, the decision to pursue higher education comes down to practical questions. Can they afford the fees? Can they travel to classes regularly? Can they continue working while studying? These questions can be especially difficult for school leavers who live far from a campus and for adults balancing work and family responsibilities. Inspire College’s online model is designed to give these learners a way to study from where they live and fit their education around existing commitments.

Inspire College offers pathways from foundation and higher diploma through degree and master’s-level study. Its programmes cover areas including business, computing, health science, teaching and law. Eligible students can begin a foundation programme after their O/Ls, giving them an entry point into higher education and a route to further study. Working adults can choose a pathway that suits their existing qualifications and career goals while continuing in employment. Across its programmes, the college combines academic study with industry-linked learning and aims to keep fees affordable.

Part of the investment will fund an AI-enabled learning management system designed to support students throughout their studies. For an online college, the learning platform is where much of the day-to-day student experience happens. It is where learners access course material and return to their studies around work and family commitments. Strengthening that platform gives Inspire College a way to improve the experience for students from the time they begin a programme through to completion.

The investment will also support the use of conversational AI to make onboarding simpler and faster. New students often have practical questions about what to do after enrolling, how to get started, and where to find information. Making those first steps easier to navigate can help students begin their studies with a clearer understanding of what comes next.

Alongside the technology investment, Inspire College plans to expand outreach in regional cities. Online delivery makes it possible to study from home, but prospective students still need clear information about entry requirements, available programmes and how they can progress from one qualification to the next. Regional outreach will help more school leavers and working adults find out which pathways are open to them without having to travel to a major city to explore their options.

The partnership gives Inspire College the resources to reach more learners and improve the experience they have once they enrol. For a school leaver in a regional town or a working parent studying in the evenings, the goal is the same: a practical route to a recognised qualification that fits the life they already lead.

data.title: Inspire College Hosts Financial Literacy Workshop with Bhanuka Harischandra
data.excerpt: Inspire College hosted an in-person Financial Literacy Workshop in Colombo, led by Bhanuka Harischandra. The one-day session introduced participants to the college’s Financial Literacy & Wealth Building programme.
content: Inspire College held its Financial Literacy Workshop on Sunday, 18 October 2026, at the DHPL Conference Centre on Nawam Mawatha, Colombo. Led by Bhanuka Harischandra, Director of Inspire College and founder of Surge Global, the in-person workshop gave participants a chance to experience the Financial Literacy & Wealth Building programme before deciding whether to pursue the full course.
## Making financial literacy practical

Financial decisions often begin with everyday questions. How much of your income goes towards fixed expenses? What room is there to save? How can you work towards a longer-term goal while managing the commitments you have today? Inspire College’s Financial Literacy & Wealth Building programme is designed to help learners approach those questions with a clearer understanding of how they earn, spend, save and plan.

The workshop brought that learning into an in-person setting. The one-day format gave participants a focused introduction to the programme and a chance to consider how the subject relates to their own circumstances. Someone early in their career might be thinking about how to manage a regular salary. Someone supporting a household or running a business might already be balancing several financial commitments and want a clearer way to set priorities.
## From earning income to planning for the future

Bhanuka’s teaching materials for the wider programme cover three connected areas: increasing income, investing the difference between income and expenses, and developing a personal wealth strategy. Together, they frame financial literacy as a skill that develops over time, through decisions about earning, managing what comes in and setting aside money for future goals.

The programme connects those topics to choices learners are likely to encounter in their own lives. Exploring ways to increase income, for example, starts with understanding what skills someone already has and where those skills could create new opportunities. Setting a longer-term goal starts with understanding current expenses and what someone can realistically set aside. These questions give learners a starting point for developing a plan that reflects their own priorities.
## A first step into the full programme

The workshop was designed as a standalone introduction for people who wanted to explore the subject before committing to a longer course. It also gave prospective learners a way to get familiar with Inspire College’s approach to teaching financial literacy and consider whether the broader programme aligned with what they wanted to learn.

For Inspire College, the session was an opportunity to connect professional development with decisions people make outside the classroom. Financial literacy is relevant when someone starts a job, takes on new responsibilities, considers a business idea or begins planning for a personal goal. The workshop gave participants a place to start thinking through those decisions and a pathway to continue learning through the Financial Literacy & Wealth Building programme.

data.title: ATHE UK CEO Alex Birks Visits Inspire College
data.excerpt: ATHE UK CEO Alex Birks Visits Inspire College, Strengthening International Academic Collaboration
content: ATHE UK CEO Alex Birks Visits Inspire College, Strengthening International Academic Collaboration

Inspire College welcomed Alex Birks, Chief Executive Officer of ATHE (Awards for Training and Higher Education), UK, to Colombo for a strategic meeting with the college's leadership, marking an important milestone in its commitment to making internationally recognised higher education more accessible to Sri Lankan learners.

The visit reflected the growing relationship between Inspire College and ATHE, a UK-based awarding organisation regulated by the Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation (Ofqual). It provided an opportunity to discuss the future of higher education, international academic pathways, and the role of technology in creating more flexible learning experiences.
Strengthening International Academic Partnerships

During his visit, Alex Birks engaged with the Inspire College leadership team, discussing opportunities to strengthen academic collaboration and expand access to internationally recognised qualifications.

As an ATHE-recognised centre, Inspire College offers learners access to UK-regulated qualifications across several academic and professional disciplines. The collaboration supports students seeking flexible educational pathways while balancing employment, personal responsibilities, and career development.
The meeting highlighted a shared interest in developing accessible, career-relevant education that responds to the changing needs of students and employers.
Transforming Higher Education Through Digital Learning
Inspire College is committed to reshaping traditional higher education through its 100% online learning model.

By combining digital learning resources, recorded lessons, interactive live sessions, and structured academic support, Inspire College enables students to pursue their qualifications without the geographical and scheduling limitations often associated with conventional classroom-based education.
The visit provided an opportunity to highlight Inspire College's approach to digital education and its vision of bringing international academic opportunities closer to Sri Lankan learners.
Creating Pathways to International Qualifications
Through its relationship with ATHE, Inspire College provides academic progression opportunities that can support learners at different stages of their educational and professional journeys.

These pathways include foundation-level qualifications, higher diploma-level studies, and postgraduate-level qualifications in fields such as Business and Management, Computing, and other professional disciplines.
Eligible students completing relevant ATHE qualifications may also explore progression opportunities through participating university partners, subject to the applicable entry requirements.
The relationship between ATHE and Inspire College represents an important part of the college's broader mission to make quality international education more accessible, affordable, and flexible.
A Shared Vision for the Future of Education
Alex Birks' visit reinforced the importance of collaboration between international awarding organisations and innovative education providers.

As Inspire College continues to expand its academic portfolio and strengthen its international relationships, the institution remains focused on delivering meaningful learning experiences, supporting professional development, and creating opportunities for lifelong education.
The visit represents another step in Inspire College's journey towards building a digitally connected higher education ecosystem that serves learners in Sri Lanka and beyond.
Inspire College — Learn Without Limits.

data.title: Inspire College Partners with ATHE to Deliver Globally Recognised UK Qualifications in Sri Lanka
data.excerpt: Inspire College is proud to announce its partnership with Awards for Training and Higher Education (ATHE), a leading UK awarding organisation regulated by Ofqual. This collaboration brings world-class Business, Management, and Computing qualifications to Sri Lankan students, providing a seamless pathway from local study to internationally recognised degrees.
content:
ATHE: Excellence in Global Education
ATHE is renowned for delivering high-quality, flexible, and career-focused qualifications in over 40 countries. From Level 3 diplomas to Level 7 postgraduate equivalents, ATHE equips students with the academic foundation and practical skills that universities and employers value worldwide.
By studying ATHE programs at Inspire College, students gain access to:
Internationally recognised qualifications that meet UK standards
Flexible learning options tailored to modern student lifestyles
Clear pathways to progression at UK and international universities

Ofqual: Ensuring Quality and Global Recognition
Ofqual, (Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation), is the official regulator of qualifications, exams, and assessments in England. It ensures that qualifications meet strict quality standards so they are reliable, credible, and respected globally.
Here’s why Ofqual matters for students:
Quality Assurance: All qualifications regulated by Ofqual are regularly reviewed and monitored. This ensures consistent academic standards and fair assessment practices.
International Recognition: An Ofqual-regulated qualification is trusted worldwide. Universities and employers recognise it as credible evidence of your knowledge and skills.
Clear Progression: Qualifications approved by Ofqual are designed to support pathways to higher education, including UK Top-Up degrees, postgraduate programs, and professional opportunities.
Student Confidence: Being Ofqual-regulated gives students and parents confidence that the program meets high academic and professional standards.

For ATHE students, this means the diplomas and extended diplomas they complete at Inspire College are rigorously assessed, globally recognised, and fully credible for progression to UK partner universities or international career paths.

Your Gateway to a UK Top-Up Degree
One of the key advantages of ATHE programs is the progression route to a UK Top-Up Degree.
Students who complete an ATHE Diploma or Extended Diploma at Inspire College can advance to the final year of a degree with ATHE’s UK university partners. This pathway allows students to:
Begin their studies locally in Sri Lanka
Earn a globally recognised ATHE qualification
Progress seamlessly to a UK Top-Up Degree, opening doors to international career opportunities

Why Choose ATHE at Inspire College?
Studying ATHE programs with Inspire College offers a truly future-focused education experience:
Live, interactive classes with experienced faculty
Industry-relevant curriculum aligned with global trends
Flexible online and blended learning options
Affordable access to UK-standard qualifications without relocating
Strong university progression opportunities for degree and postgraduate study

Building Skills for Global Success
ATHE qualifications go beyond academics. They develop essential real-world skills, including critical thinking, problem-solving, leadership, and communication.
At Inspire College, students not only achieve internationally recognised qualifications but also gain the confidence and competencies to excel in today’s competitive global job market.

With Inspire College leading the way, students in Sri Lanka now have access to globally recognised qualifications, clear pathways to UK Top-Up degrees, and a future-focused education that emphasizes innovation, critical thinking, and real-world readiness — marking a new chapter in Sri Lanka’s higher education journey.

data.title: Steven Enderby — our new Chairman
data.excerpt:
25+ years in private equity, strategy and governance Steven Enderby (Chairman)



- Steven Enderby, Chairman of Inspire College, is a seasoned leader with 25+ years in private equity, strategy, and governance. Former CEO of Hemas Holdings PLC with senior roles at Actis LLP and CDC Capital Partners, he leverages deep regional experience to advance Inspire College’s innovative, accessible education mission
content: Steven Enderby is the Chairman of Inspire College. He brings more than 25 years of experience in private equity, corporate strategy and governance, including six years as Group CEO of Hemas Holdings PLC. Much of his career has been spent working with businesses in Sri Lanka and India, giving him a regional perspective on how organisations grow, make long-term decisions and stay accountable as they expand.
From private equity to corporate leadership

Before joining Hemas, Steven held senior investment roles at CDC Capital Partners and Actis LLP. He was a partner at Actis from its formation in the early 2000s until 2011. His work took him across several markets, with much of his investment experience concentrated in Sri Lanka and India.

In Sri Lanka, Steven led private equity transactions involving South Asia Gateway Terminals, Ceylon Oxygen and Millennium Information Technologies. Those investments spanned port infrastructure, industrial gases and technology, giving him experience with businesses that had different customers, capital needs and plans for growth. He also served on the boards of companies including John Keells Holdings, Lion Brewery and Punjab Tractors.
Leading Hemas Holdings PLC

Steven joined Hemas Holdings in 2013 to lead the Group’s work in mergers and acquisitions and strategy. He became Deputy CEO and a director later that year and was appointed Group CEO in April 2014. He held the role until 2020, leading a Sri Lankan group with significant businesses in consumer products and healthcare.

His move from private equity to executive leadership brought a different set of responsibilities. At Hemas, his work extended from evaluating investments to leading the organisation that would carry out those decisions. That experience is relevant to a growing education provider, where decisions about what to offer, whom to partner with and where to invest have to translate into a reliable experience for learners.

Steven also serves as Non-Executive Chairman of Ironwood Capital Partners and has advised businesses in Sri Lanka and India. He holds a degree in Economics and Accounting from Queen’s University Belfast and a master’s degree in Development Studies from the University of Melbourne.
Chairing Inspire College

As Chairman, Steven brings his experience in strategy and board governance to Inspire College’s work of widening access to higher education through online learning. The college’s model is designed for learners whose choices may be shaped by where they live, the hours they work or the responsibilities they have at home. For those learners, flexibility matters alongside the quality of teaching and a clear understanding of where a qualification can lead.

As Inspire College develops its programmes and academic partnerships, the board’s role includes setting long-term direction and providing oversight. Steven’s background as an investor, chief executive and board chair gives him experience assessing how organisations can grow while staying focused on the people they serve. At Inspire College, that perspective supports the college’s aim of making higher education more accessible and relevant to Sri Lankan learners.

data.title: Inspire College Signs MoU with Allianz to Support Staff Development
data.excerpt: Inspire College and Allianz have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to support professional development for Allianz staff, with a focus on practical learning that employees can pursue alongside work.
content: Inspire College and Allianz have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to support professional development for Allianz staff. The signing formalises discussions between the two organisations about how Inspire College can support employees who want to build skills relevant to their work.

Representatives from both organisations came together for the signing, which marks the start of a collaboration focused on workplace learning. The agreement provides a basis for shaping training around the needs of Allianz teams and the day-to-day responsibilities of the people taking part.
## Bringing professional development closer to the workplace

For employees, the value of a training programme often becomes clear when they can apply what they have learned to a familiar task. A team member might want to present information more clearly, feel more confident using a digital tool or find a better way to organise a recurring piece of work. Starting with those kinds of tasks helps connect professional development to what employees actually do.

The collaboration gives Allianz and Inspire College a way to discuss which skills would benefit staff and how training can be organised around their work. Allianz can bring insight into the needs of its teams, while Inspire College brings experience in designing and delivering flexible learning. That combination can help shape training that reflects both the organisation’s priorities and the practical needs of employees.
## Learning that fits alongside work

Employees considering professional development often need to weigh the relevance of a course against the time it takes to complete. Training needs to be specific enough to be useful and structured in a way that people can follow alongside their responsibilities.

Inspire College’s approach to flexible learning can support that balance. A focused course gives learners time to explore a topic, practise a skill and consider how to use it in their own role. Employees can bring questions from work into their learning and take ideas back to their teams. Over time, that exchange can help teams identify which skills are making a difference and where further training would be useful.
## Connecting education with industry

The Allianz MoU is part of Inspire College’s work with employers to connect learning with workplace needs. Conversations with industry help the college understand where employees want to develop their skills and what makes training practical for people who are already working. For employers, working with an education provider offers a way to turn those priorities into structured learning opportunities.

The signing gives both organisations a starting point for that work. As the collaboration develops, the focus will be on identifying professional development opportunities that make sense for Allianz staff and giving employees a clear way to apply what they learn in their roles.

data.title: Inspire College Offers CPD-Certified Short Courses
data.excerpt: Build practical workplace skills with Inspire College’s online CPD-certified short courses in AI, digital marketing, data and finance
content: Inspire College is a member of The CPD Certification Service and offers online short courses for learners looking to develop practical skills in artificial intelligence, digital marketing, data and finance. The membership is part of Inspire College’s focus on professional development for students, working professionals and entrepreneurs who want to apply what they learn in their studies, workplaces or businesses.
What the CPD relationship means for learners

CPD stands for Continuing Professional Development. It describes the learning people undertake throughout their careers to build skills, update their knowledge and respond to changes in their work. For a marketing professional, that could mean learning how to evaluate a digital campaign. For an HR professional, it could mean learning how to use AI tools to prepare recruitment materials. For a business owner, it could mean becoming more confident with budgeting and financial decisions.

The CPD Certification Service independently reviews learning activities submitted for certification. The CPD Member badge identifies Inspire College’s membership with the organisation. When a specific course is listed as CPD-certified, that certification applies to the learning activity. Learners can check the individual course page for its delivery format, completion requirements and certificate details before enrolling.
Practical learning in AI and beyond

AI Mastery is one example of how Inspire College approaches professional development. The programme is designed for learners who want to understand and use AI in a business or workplace setting. It covers generative AI, prompting, productivity tools and responsible AI adoption. Learners work through business scenarios and develop a final applied use case, giving them the opportunity to relate what they learn to a specific task or challenge.

AI for HR takes a more specialised approach. It explores how AI tools can support common HR activities such as drafting job descriptions and preparing interview guides. The focus is on familiar tasks that learners can recognise from their work or use to build experience in the field.

Inspire College’s short course offering also covers digital marketing, data and finance. These areas address different workplace needs. A learner interested in marketing may want to plan content or measure campaign performance. Someone working with data may want to interpret reports and communicate findings more clearly. A learner interested in finance may want to build confidence working with budgets and costs.
Professional development that fits around work and study

Online delivery gives learners more flexibility to pursue a focused area of study alongside their existing commitments. Someone already working in marketing might start with a skill they need for an upcoming campaign. A student preparing for a first role might focus on learning tools they are likely to encounter at work. An entrepreneur might choose finance or AI based on an immediate need in their business.

Inspire College’s CPD membership and online short course offering bring two elements of professional development together: a way to access focused training and a clear basis for checking whether a particular course has been independently reviewed for CPD certification.
Explore the Inspire College Short Courses page to compare programmes and speak with an admissions adviser about the course that fits your goals.

data.title: Dinesh Kumara, Founder and CEO of Inspire College
data.excerpt: After a decade of bootstrapping ventures in Sri Lanka, Dinesh Kumara brought his experience in digital strategy and business innovation to higher education. As Founder and CEO of Inspire College, he is building flexible online study pathways for Sri Lankan learners.
content: Dinesh Kumara is the Founder and CEO of Inspire College, a Sri Lankan higher education provider built around flexible online learning. He founded the college to address a practical challenge: how can students pursue higher education when work, family responsibilities or distance make it difficult to attend a physical campus? His answer draws on the experience of building businesses across digital strategy, travel technology and healthcare, and on a belief that the way a service is delivered can determine who gets to use it.
Building businesses from the ground up

Dinesh describes the first decade of his entrepreneurial journey as bootstrapped. His ventures include Inspire X, which works with organisations on digital strategy and business model innovation, Niwadu in travel technology, and HealthX in healthcare. Each operates in a different industry, but the work starts with a similar question: where do people encounter difficulty when trying to use a service, and what would make that experience easier?

That perspective matters in higher education. A programme may be a good academic fit, but a prospective student still has to consider whether they can attend classes, manage the cost of travel or relocation, and keep up with their studies alongside other commitments. Building Inspire College around online learning puts those considerations at the centre of how the college delivers its programmes.
Giving learners more ways to pursue higher education

A school leaver exploring higher education and a working professional considering postgraduate study are making different decisions. The school leaver may want a clear entry point and an understanding of what qualification they can work towards next. The working professional may already know their field and need a way to study while continuing in employment. Inspire College offers pathways at different stages of higher education so learners can look for a starting point that fits their qualifications and goals.

Online delivery also changes the options available to students who live outside Colombo. For someone who would otherwise need to travel regularly or move closer to campus, studying online can reduce those geographical barriers. The decision to pursue a qualification can then depend more on the programme itself and how it fits the learner’s circumstances.
Developing international academic partnerships

Dinesh’s work as CEO includes building relationships with international academic partners. During a visit to the Norwich headquarters of Awards for Training and Higher Education (ATHE), he met with the organisation’s team to discuss education technology, the range of ATHE qualifications offered through Inspire College and engagement with ATHE’s university partners.

The discussion illustrates two aspects of building an online college. One is the qualification pathway and where it can lead. The other is the experience students have while studying, from how they access learning materials to how they engage with teaching and complete their assessments. Both shape whether a programme is a good fit for a learner.

In his public writing, Dinesh describes working with strategic partners as the next stage of his entrepreneurial journey. After years of building ventures independently, he now works with partners across Sri Lanka and the United Kingdom who bring expertise, networks and a shared long-term vision.
Supporting entrepreneurs beyond his own businesses

Dinesh’s interest in entrepreneurship also extends to the opportunities available to other founders. He has shared his involvement with Sri Lanka’s National Enterprise Development Authority and his participation in a SAARC delegation to the Commonwealth Secretariat. The discussions he highlighted included support for young entrepreneurs, greater participation for women in business and improved access to opportunities for people with disabilities.

His work across entrepreneurship and education returns to a common concern: whether people can access the training, relationships and institutions that help them take the next step. At Inspire College, that means building study options for learners with different starting points and making it easier for them to see how one stage of their education can lead to the next.
